title: Trajan becomes emperor
text: Nerva had adopted Trajan in 97 and died in January 98. Trajan was in Germany when the news reached him (at Cologne, according to Eutropius). He stayed on the Rhine and Danube frontiers for more than a year and only arrived in Rome in 99.

title: First Dacian War
place: Tapae, near the Iron Gates of Transylvania pass (approximate)
text: Trajan crossed the Danube to fight King Decebalus of Dacia and won a hard battle at Tapae in 101. The fighting went on into the next year, until Decebalus asked for peace in 102 and agreed to rule as a king loyal to Rome.

title: Second Dacian War
text: Decebalus didn’t keep the peace for long, so Trajan came back in 105, this time crossing the Danube on Apollodorus’ new bridge at Drobeta. The Dacian capital, Sarmizegetusa Regia, fell in 106. Decebalus killed himself rather than be caught, and Dacia became a Roman province.

title: Arabia annexed
text: When Rabbel II, the last king of the Nabataeans, died, the governor of Syria, Aulus Cornelius Palma, took over his kingdom, probably with little or no fighting. It became the province of Arabia, with its capital at Bostra. That’s why the coins say Arabia was “acquired” (adquisita) and not conquered.

title: Trajan’s Column dedicated
text: The column, carved with the story of the Dacian Wars, was dedicated in May 113 in the new Forum of Trajan. That autumn Trajan left Rome for the East, and he never came back.

title: Armenia annexed
text: Rome and Parthia had agreed that Armenia’s king would be a Parthian prince approved by Rome, but Parthia crowned Parthamasiris without asking. Trajan marched in. At Elegeia he refused to accept Parthamasiris, who was killed soon after, and Armenia was made a Roman province.

title: Earthquake at Antioch
text: Trajan was spending the winter at Antioch when a huge earthquake wrecked the city, probably in December 115. Cassius Dio says Trajan climbed out through a window with only minor injuries, but many people died, including one of the consuls.

title: Ctesiphon taken
text: Trajan marched down the Euphrates and the Tigris and captured the Parthian capital, Ctesiphon, in 116. That was the year he took the title Parthicus, “conqueror of the Parthians”, and announced two new provinces, Mesopotamia and Assyria.

title: Trajan reaches the Persian Gulf
text: He sailed on to the top of the Persian Gulf, where the king of Characene surrendered to him. Cassius Dio says that when Trajan watched a ship leave for India, he wished he were young enough to follow Alexander the Great. But revolts were already breaking out behind him.

title: Death at Selinus
text: Trajan failed to take the desert city of Hatra and fell ill. He set out for Rome, but he had a stroke and died at Selinus in Cilicia in early August 117. Hadrian, who was said to have been adopted on Trajan’s deathbed, took over and soon gave up Armenia, Mesopotamia and Assyria.
